title: Phytochrome Activities and Biological Activities of Genes for Phytochrome A of Horseradish in Horseradish Hairy Roots.
why: Armoracia sense_light_nonvisual: the harvest (run 3, query "Armoracia phytochrome photoreceptor") lists this Plant Biotechnology paper (2003), whose abstract start says full-length horseradish phytochrome A cDNAs under the CaMV 35S promoter were put into horseradish hairy roots, raising phytochrome levels two- to threefold, and that the phytochromes were photochemically active; the "biological activities" of the title may be light-dependent growth responses of the roots. The desk-screen searches "Armoracia light intensity OR shade OR photoperiod growth" and "horseradish light intensity OR shade OR photoperiod growth" returned only general photoperiod and growing-guide pages. Harvest-c23 named this work for the next unit. One fork stays open for the owner: a hairy-root culture is transformed tissue grown apart from the plant, which reading 10(a) may treat as tissue taken from the plant. Nothing was opened; the authors were not shown.

title: Morphological dynamics of flower development and sex differentiation in monoecious soapberry (Sapindus mukorossi Gaertn.)
why: Sapindus diel: the desk-screen search "Sapindus flower opening time anthesis" returned this Industrial Crops and Products article (ScienceDirect pii S0926669025012701) on flower development and sex differentiation in Sapindus mukorossi; a staged account of flower development in a monoecious tree often times anthesis and anther dehiscence within the day, so it may give the hour at which soapberry flowers open. The companion search "western soapberry flower opening time anthesis" returned only species and nursery pages. Nothing was opened; no authors, year or DOI were shown.

title: Spatial and Temporal Variability of the Floral Scent Emitted by Barlia robertiana (Loisel.) Greuter, a Mediterranean Food-Deceptive Orchid
why: Himantoglossum sense_chemical and diel: the desk-screen search "Himantoglossum floral scent volatiles" returned this Compounds article; Barlia robertiana is Himantoglossum robertianum, the queue species. A floral scent emitted by a food-deceptive orchid is a volatile signal of the kind main logs under sense_chemical, and "temporal variability" may include the timing of emission within the day, which audit 80's desk ruling counts as plant diel. Audit 80's desk ruling holds scent sampled from cut flowers to be excised tissue under reading 10(a), so whether the flowers were sampled on the living plant decides the reading. Nothing was opened; no authors or year were shown.
